LESSON: SIGN READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Sign Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: how they can use the selected reading strategies. 1. Why should one sign read for main ideas? 2. How can you improve your reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: Learners develop the skill of organising their own learning as they share what they have learnt while completing a

mind map focusing on the main idea and details.

● Digital literacy : Learners develop interacting with digital skills as they manipulate digital devices while searching online and watching

appropriate video clips on the selected reading strategies.

Values:
● Unity: is achieved as learners work together to complete the mind map.

Link to other Subjects

● The learner is able to relate the skills used in intensive reading to their learning of comprehension in Kiswahili or Kenya Sign Language

Suggested Learning Resources

Word cards, Chart, Class readers, Adapted Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g. tablets and mobile phones, Dictionary,
